data.title: J&J touts spinal pain, stiffness improvements with Tremfya
data.description:
• Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) said that phase 4 data on Tremfya (guselkumab) showed that the IL-23 antagonist led to significant reductions in pain, stiffness, swelling, and fatigue in patients with psoriatic arthritis and axial involvement.
  • At week 24 of the STAR study, mean Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) scores improved by −3.3 (on a 10-point scale) with Tremfya 100 mg every four weeks and −2.9 with Tremfya every eight weeks vs. −2.1 with placebo.
  • MRI-assessed sacroiliac joint inflammation, measured by the Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada (SPARCC) score, found Tremfya reduced scores by −7.1 and −5.2, respectively, compared to −2.4 with placebo.
  • Also, those on Tremfya saw excellent skin clearance compared to those on placebo, confirming results found in other studies.

data.title: S&P 500 is on track for the worst week since the April 2025 'Liberation Day' sell-off
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is heading into Friday’s trading session under significant downward pressure, already lower by 5.1% for the week.

S&P futures (SPX) point to an opening decline of roughly -1%, raising the possibility that the benchmark will close out one of its weakest weeks in recent memory.

If the index holds near current levels, the week would rank as the worst since the Liberation Day sell-off of April 2025. The broader picture is equally sobering. The S&P 500 has now fallen in six straight sessions—its longest such streak since April 2024. A seventh consecutive decline on Friday would extend the losing run to levels not seen since the sharp market drop that began in February 2020 at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The combination of a multi-day losing streak and a weekly decline exceeding 5% underscores the intensity of the recent selling. Investors will be watching closely to see whether the index can stabilize or whether the current downward momentum continues through the final session of the week.

data.title: TD Cowen backs UnitedHealth & Humana with buy upgrades, shares rise
data.description:
Shares of UnitedHealth (UNH) and Humana (HUM) ticked up in premarket trading on Friday after TD Cowen upgraded both health insurers to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’, citing an improved outlook and scope for further upside. Target price on UNH raised to $455 from $402, which implies a 38% increase from last closing price.

For UnitedHealth (UNH), TD Cowen analyst Ryan Langston sees the stock as an attractive story, with a credible path toward mid-high-teens EPS growth through 2028.

“We see a credible path toward mid-high-teens EPS growth through at least 2028 given Medicare Advantage benefit design, Optum Health recovery & Commercial/Medicaid improvement”.

The brokerage notes that recent CRUSH proposals and potential for further regulatory/congressional impact are important near-term debates. Additionally, TD Cowen said continued external growth at Optum Rx and commercialization of Optum Insight’s AI-first products are areas to watch.

 

 

For Humana on the other hand, Langston sees a relatively clear path towards a meaningful step-up in 2027 EPS growth and a greater than $40 EPS in 2028.

“Our 2027 MA benefits analysis suggests major carriers, including HUM, broadly prioritized profitability recovery over enrollment for 2027, reducing the risk that HUM is competitively disadvantaged by its pricing actions,” the analyst noted.

Sees potential for HUM to raise its prior operating leverage framework at its Dec. 10 investor update, as it lifted PT to $485 from $430, which implies a 28% increase from last closing price. HUM was about ~2% before the opening bell.

data.title: Anthropic's aggregate gross proceeds reach $93.5B from landmark IPO
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) generated $93.5B in aggregated gross proceeds from its landmark initial public offering on Thursday.

After deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses, Anthropic received $91.6B, the AI lab reported on Friday.

Anthropic also closed the concurrent sale of an aggregate of 313.25M shares of Class N common stock to Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Google (GOOG)(GOOGL), Micron Technology (MU), Microsoft (MSFT), NVIDIA (NVDA), and TSMC (TSM) at the public offering price of $83 per share, in a private placement for an aggregate purchase price of $26B. 

Aggregate gross proceeds from the IPO, including the shares sold by the selling stockholders, and the concurrent private placement totaled $119.5B.

The Claude maker's historic IPO shadowed the previous record set by SpaceX (SPCX) in June, which raised a total of $86.25B, including additional shares sold by underwriters through the overallotment option.

However, shares had plunged 13% during pre-market trading on Friday, dragging the stock near its initial pricing of $83. It opened on Thursday at $111.50 but closed at $97.17, or 17% more than its initial pricing.

Goldman Sachs Group (GS), Morgan Stanley (MS), and 20 other banks earned a record $550M in fees for their work on Anthropic's IPO.

"For the first time a U.S. frontier lab carries a standalone public market price, uncluttered by an ad business or a rocket business, and the anchor roster tells the story," said Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives in an investor note. "Nvidia and Google lead the placement at $10 billion each with AMD and four more suppliers and clouds behind them, which means the capex cycle the hyperscalers reported earlier this month and the demand Anthropic is contracting for are the same dollars viewed from both ends."

"The $900.9 billion of aggregate compute commitments disclosed in the November 10 amendment, of which $70.7 billion falls due in the next 12 months, is a multi-year demand signal for chipmakers and the clouds that host them, and investors can now underwrite it from a public filing rather than infer it from capex guides," he added. "The debate from here is margin against growth, as revenue compounding more than twelvefold y/y while prices fall and compute costs run ahead of recognition captures the frontier lab business model in a single P&L, and the shares will be judged on whether the operating profit of the second quarter or the loss of the third is the run-rate."

data.title: PayPal's new CFO to get up to $31M in stock and bonuses
data.description:
Claire Bramley, who becomes PayPal Holdings' (PYPL) chief financial officer on Feb. 3, 2027, will get up to $31M  in bonuses and restricted stock, the company disclosed in a filing on Friday. That amount comes on top of her $875K annual base salary.

Bramley joins the company from Xero, an accounting software company, where she served as CFO from April 2025. She also served as interim chief people officer of Xero as of June 2026.

The new PayPal CFO will get:

  • A one-time cash signing bonus of $5M, payable in two installments;
  • Restricted stock units, or RSUs, having a targeted grant date value of $6M; 
  • Sign-on restricted stock units (sign-on RSUs) having a targeted grant date value of $14M; and
  • Performance-based restricted stock units, PBRSUs, having a targeted grant date value of $6M.

One-third of the RSUs will invest on Bramley's first anniversary of the grant date with 1/12th vesting each quarter thereafter.

For the $14M sign-on RSUs, $7.5M will vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, with the rest vesting on the second anniversary.

The PBRSUs for 2027 will vest on the same schedule as the company's other senior executives.

PayPal (PYPL) stock dropped 3.7% in premarket trading.

data.title: BJ's Wholesale Club's upside stalls as one-offs and promo costs offset upbeat outlook
data.description:
BJ’s Wholesale Club (BJ) beat expectations on nearly every metric in the third quarter, as higher membership fee income, increased traffic, and digitally enabled sales pushed revenue and earnings per share above Wall Street forecasts. 

The company also raised its outlook for fiscal year 2026, with EPS now seen between $5.10 and $5.30 and comparable sales (ex-gasoline) up 2.5% to 3.0%. This compares to a prior outlook for EPS of $4.60 and $4.80 and comparable sales of 2.0% to 3.0%. The current EPS forecast compares to an estimate of $4.73 and the comparable sales estimate of 2.55%.

In addition to better-than-expected top- and bottom-line, BJ’s Wholesale Club (BJ) topped expectations for comparable store sales in the third quarter. Excluding gasoline sales, comparable store sales were up 13.5%, while sales excluding gasoline rose 4.1% versus estimates of up 2.9%. 

Shares were in the red ahead of Friday’s open, however, as higher costs, increased promotions during the company’s birthday celebration, and operational costs associated with new stores weighed on the company’s gross profit margin, while an increased dependence on membership fees raised concerns about future profitability, especially with the stock hovering near a 19-month high and in the green for 10 consecutive weeks.  

The results also reflect a pre-tax benefit of ~$145M related to a litigation settlement tied to credit card interchange fees. This was only partially offset by $95M of expenses tied to the use of these proceeds. Gains associated with sale-leaseback transactions during Q2 also gave a boost to the company’s bottom-line, all of which left shares down as much as 6% in Friday’s premarket trading and put BJ’s stock at risk to trade lower for a fourth consecutive day.
